title.narrative: Nutrition Smart CommUnity in Sierra Leone Year 2

description.narrative: The Nutrition Smart Community project targets vulnerable households in rural chiefdoms of Barri and Makpele chiefdoms in the Pujehun district and Lokomasama and Kamasondo chiefdoms in Port Loko District.Barri Chiefdom with a population of 36,905 (17,697 males and 19,208 females), Makpele Chiefdom with a population of 13,080 (15,425 males and 15,655 females), out of a total district population of 346,461 (168,869 males and 177,592 females) of the Pujehun district. Lokomasama Chiefdom has a population of 48,293 ( 25,415 females + 22,878 males) and Kamasondo a population of 29,983 ( 15,530 females + 14,453 males) out of a total population of 530,865 ( 275,835 females + 255,030 males ) people in Port Loko District.

This is the 2nd year of a 3-year project (01/11/2021 -31/12/2024) with annual appropriations from the donor. (Irish Aid). It is implemented together with Concern World Wide whereas WHH is the lead. The project is in its 2nd year of rolling out the Nutrition Smart CommUnity approaching 2 districts in Sierra Leone. It builds on the Linking Agriculture with Natural Resource Management and Nutrition (LANN+) approach developed by Welthungerhilfe in cooperation with other NGOs and aims at tackling malnutrition through systematic screening and conducting nutrition camps.

This is the 2nd year of a 3-year project.Objective : To improve household Food and Nutrition Security among vulnerable households in Pujehun and Port Loko districts in Sierra LeoneOutcomes:(1)Knowledge, awareness and practices of extension workers and relevant authorities as well as target households on diet diversity, maternal-child care, nutrition sensitive agriculture and WASH are improved(2)Dietary diversity of households, particularly women and children, is increased through promotion of nutrition sensitive and climate smart organic agriculture.(3)Community based organizations, community level institutions, local government bodies and private sector actors in target areas are capacitated to access government programs and entitlements as well as access private sector services.(4)Enhanced access of government and development actors to data, evidence, information and knowledge on replicable models to guide multi-sectoral programming towards better nutrition.
